# Output-variable reference

How Abaqus field/history output identifiers map to CalculiX `*NODE FILE` / `*EL FILE` / `*NODE PRINT` / `*EL PRINT` variables.

## Renamed / folded onto a CalculiX identifier

| Abaqus | CalculiX |
| --- | --- |
| `CEEQ` | `PEEQ` |
| `EE` | `ME` |
| `LE` | `E` |
| `NE11` | `E` |
| `NT11` | `NT` |
| `PE` | `PEEQ` |
| `PEMAG` | `PEEQ` |
| `RM` | `RF` |
| `RT` | `RF` |
| `UR` | `U` |
| `UT` | `U` |

## Dropped — no CalculiX equivalent (derive in post-processing)

`A`, `AENER`, `AREA`, `AT`, `CDISP`, `CELENT`, `CF`, `CFORCE`, `COORD`, `CSTRESS`, `CTF`, `DAMAGEC`, `DAMAGEFC`, `DAMAGEFT`, `DAMAGEMC`, `DAMAGEMT`, `DAMAGESHR`, `DAMAGET`, `DMICRT`, `DUCTCRT`, `ELEDEN`, `ELEN`, `EPDDEN`, `ESEDEN`, `EVF`, `EVOLAVG`, `IE`, `LODE`, `MISES`, `MMIXDME`, `NE`, `NFLUX`, `NFORC`, `PEEQVAVG`, `PEVAVG`, `PHILSM`, `PRESS`, `PSILSM`, `RBFOR`, `SDEG`, `SE`, `SF`, `SM`, `STATUS`, `STATUSXFEM`, `STH`, `SVAVG`, `TEMP`, `TRESC`, `TRIAX`, `VENER`

## Valid only on `*EL PRINT` / `*NODE PRINT` (.dat)

Dropped from `*EL FILE`/`*NODE FILE` (.frd): `CELS`, `ELKE`, `ELSE`, `EVOL`.

## Energies from the first step

ccx 2.23 computes element energies from the first step that needs them on — an implicit `*DYNAMIC` or a transient coupled temperature-displacement step, or a request for `CELS`, `ELKE`, `ELSE`, `ENER` — and in a nonlinear calculation stops when that is not the first step. The converter then adds `ENER` to the first step's `*EL FILE` (or an `*EL FILE` card for it), and keeps it out of the steps after it, into which ccx would carry it.

## Preselected field output (`*OUTPUT, FIELD, VARIABLE=PRESELECT`)

Abaqus' preselected field output per procedure (Analysis User's Guide, *Output to the output database*, table 1) as the whole-model ccx cards it becomes. Abaqus also writes it for a step without any output database request (`*OUTPUT`) when none carries over from an earlier step (requests carry over to later steps; between perturbation steps only from the step before), so the converter adds it there; `*NODE PRINT`/`*EL PRINT`/`*NODE FILE`/`*EL FILE` are .dat/.fil requests and do not replace it. Carried-over requests are written again in such a step, at their own frequency and with its procedure's variables, as ccx would keep the earlier step's frequency. `PEEQ` only where a material yields or creeps (ccx warns on it otherwise); `VARIABLE=ALL` adds `ENER`. The frequency is the `*OUTPUT` card's, else Abaqus' default: every increment, every 10 in `*DYNAMIC`/`*MODAL DYNAMIC`, 20 intervals in explicit dynamics (there a `FREQUENCY` from ccx's stable increment, as ccx ignores `*TIME POINTS`). Abaqus' preselected history output, whole-model energies, has no ccx counterpart and is dropped.

Its contact output (`CSTRESS`, `CDISP`), which Abaqus writes where the model has contact, becomes `*CONTACT FILE` (CDIS and CSTR switch on the same CONTACT block in ccx: opening, slip, pressure and shear at the slave nodes) where ccx 2.23 can write it: a model with a `*CONTACT PAIR` that is not `TIED`. Left out, with a note: general contact and tied pairs, which become no ccx contact pair (ccx would write an empty block), and node-to-surface pairs (the Abaqus default) in a model with axisymmetric elements — ccx 2.23 aborts writing their contact output once the `.frd` also gets `S` — or with plane or membrane elements and no beam or shell — ccx writes it at the nodes of their expanded 3-D form, which the 2-D `.frd` of such a model lacks. Face-to-face pairs (`SURFACE TO SURFACE`) have it in every model; none of it in linear perturbation steps (Abaqus preselects none there).

| Procedure | `*NODE FILE` | `*EL FILE` | `*CONTACT FILE` | No ccx label for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `*STATIC` | U, RF | S, E, PEEQ | CDIS, CSTR | CF |
| `*VISCO` | U, RF | S, E, PEEQ | CDIS, CSTR | CF |
| `*DYNAMIC` (implicit) | U, V, RF | S, E, PEEQ | CDIS, CSTR | A, CF |
| `*MODAL DYNAMIC` | U, V, RF | S, E | — | A, CF |
| `*STEADY STATE DYNAMICS` | U, RF | S, E | — | V, A, CF |
| `*FREQUENCY` | U | — | — | — |
| `*BUCKLE` | U | — | — | — |
| `*COMPLEX FREQUENCY` | U | — | — | — |
| `*HEAT TRANSFER` | NT, RFL | HFL | — | — |
| `*COUPLED TEMPERATURE-DISPLACEMENT` | U, RF, NT, RFL | S, E, PEEQ, HFL | CDIS, CSTR | CF |
| `*DYNAMIC, EXPLICIT` | U, V, RF | S, E, PEEQ | CSTR | A, EVF and the volume averages |

## Results digest (`--run`)

After a run that solves, `--run` prints a line or two per step, read from the `.frd` and `.dat` (`ccx_results_digest`), to set beside the Abaqus results; `--json` gives it under `results`, one object per step, with `run` (the ccx, its version, the status). Values are at the step's last increment.

| Key | What |
| --- | --- |
| `time` | the total time reached, as ccx writes it |
| `max_u`, `max_mises` | the largest \|U\| and von Mises stress and their node (`.frd`), or the printed set and node or element (`.dat`) where the `.frd` lacks them |
| `rf` | per `*BOUNDARY` target, RF summed over the DOFs 1–3 it holds; per set printed with RF, over those any BC holds there. That is what Abaqus' RF sums to: ccx's RF also holds the applied loads. From the `.dat`, else the `.frd` if it has all the nodes (it lacks reference points and shell and beam nodes) |
| `frequencies`, `buckling_factors` | of a `*FREQUENCY` (cycles/time) or `*BUCKLE` step |

A node ccx adds expanding a shell or beam is given `near` the deck's node; the converter's own nodes and elements (knot beams, skins) are left out; in an assembly `[Instance.label]` (`abaqus`) names the node, element or set as Abaqus does, from the report's instance map (`instances` in `--json`). Steady-state dynamics and complex frequency steps are not digested.
